name: SelfJoin0
label: equivalent
adaptation: schema s(??) given two columns a, b. Equivalent on every database, empty r included: the self join is empty exactly when r is, and DISTINCT removes the copies it makes.
sql_a: select distinct x.* from r x, r y
sql_b: select distinct x.* from r x

name: SelfJoin0-no-distinct
label: not_equivalent
adaptation: negative sibling: SelfJoin0 without DISTINCT. A table of n rows gives n*n rows on the left and n on the right (equal only for n = 0 or 1).
sql_a: select x.* from r x, r y

name: SelfJoin0-other-table
label: not_equivalent
adaptation: negative sibling: the join partner is another table s, so an empty s empties the left side while r stays non-empty. Only a self join can be dropped.
sql_a: select distinct x.* from r x, s y
sql_b: select distinct x.* from r x

name: productDistributesOverUnion
label: equivalent
adaptation: schemas s1(??), s2(??) given two columns each; Cosette's bare (r2 union all r3) in FROM is written as a derived table.
sql_a: select * from r1 x, (select * from r2 union all select * from r3) y
sql_b: (select * from r1 x, r2 y) union all (select * from r1 x, r3 y)

name: productDistributesOverUnion-union-distinct
label: not_equivalent
adaptation: negative sibling: UNION (duplicate-removing) on the right; a row in both r2 and r3, or a repeated r1 row, appears more often on the left.
sql_a: select * from r1 x, (select * from r2 union all select * from r3) y
sql_b: (select * from r1 x, r2 y) union (select * from r1 x, r3 y)

name: projectionDistributesOverUnion
label: equivalent
adaptation: schema s(??) given two columns a, b; Cosette's bare (r union all s) in FROM is written as a derived table.
sql_a: select * from (select * from r union all select * from s) x
sql_b: (select * from r x) union all (select * from s y)

name: projectionDistributesOverUnion-union-distinct
label: not_equivalent
adaptation: negative sibling: UNION (duplicate-removing) on the right; a repeated row or a row in both tables appears more often on the left.
sql_a: select * from (select * from r union all select * from s) x
sql_b: (select * from r x) union (select * from s y)

name: pushdownSelect
label: equivalent
adaptation: schemas s1(??), s2(??) given two columns each; the uninterpreted predicate b(s2) is the hidden column __b, as in the original conversion.
sql_a: select * from r1 x, (select * from r2 y where y.__b) z
sql_b: select * from r1 x, r2 y where y.__b

name: pushdownSelect-wrong-side
label: not_equivalent
adaptation: negative sibling: the filter is pushed into the wrong input (r1 instead of r2). A concrete predicate replaces b, because refutations of hidden-predicate cases are never claimed.
sql_a: select * from r1 x, (select * from r2 y where y.c = 1) z
sql_b: select * from r1 x, r2 y where x.a = 1
